commands: kubectl get pods -n test-social-network; kubectl get events -n test-social-network --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20

cd /tmp; kubectl get svc,ep -n test-social-network | awk '{print $1,$2,$3,$5}' | head -70; kubectl get deploy -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].ports[*].containerPort}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl get svc text-service -n test-social-network -o yaml | grep -A8 ports:
kubectl patch svc text-service -n test-social-network --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":9090}]'; kubectl get ep text-service -n test-social-network
agent.summary:
The anomaly was a misconfigured `text-service` Service. Its `targetPort` was 9999, but the container listens on 9090. Calls to it (for example, from compose-post) would have failed even though every pod showed Running.

I patched the Service's `targetPort` to 9090. Its endpoint is now `10.244.1.157:9090`. I didn't send any test requests through the app, so the fix is confirmed only by the endpoint change. All 27 pods were Running with no restarts, and I didn't check pod logs. Every other Service had endpoints, and I didn't compare their ports to their containers.
